content: I'll read the test image to analyze the visual symptoms.

**Visual Analysis:**

- **Plant part affected**: Leaf (tomato leaf based on shape)
- **Spots**: Multiple small-to-medium (~3–6 mm) dark/nearly black circular lesions scattered across the entire leaf surface
- **Spot characteristics**: Dark margins with slightly lighter (grayish) centers; some lesions show faint concentric patterning; a few spots appear to have minute dark specks within (consistent with pycnidia)
- **Grayish-white area**: Right portion of the leaf shows a significant ashy/dusty patch, consistent with advanced necrosis or dense pycnidial sporulation from Septoria lesions coalescing
- **Leaf background**: Predominantly green, indicating systemic health otherwise intact

**Differential Reasoning:**

- **Septoria Leaf Blotch** (*Septoria lycopersici*): Classic presentation — small circular spots with dark brown-black borders and gray/tan centers containing pycnidia; very common on tomato; the grayish patches align with coalescent advanced lesions. ✅ Strong match
- **Bacterial Speck**: Spots would be smaller (<2 mm) with yellow halos — spots here are larger and no clear halos. ❌
- **Early Blight**: Spots typically larger with very prominent concentric rings and yellow halo; centers are brown/tan, not nearly black. ❌
- **Target Spot**: Larger brown lesions with clearer concentric rings and yellow halo; pattern less scattered. ❌
- **Leaf Mold**: Olive-green velvety patches on underside, pale yellow patches on top — the dark discrete spots don't match. ❌

The distribution, size, color (dark borders + gray centers), and the grayish sporulation zone are all hallmarks of Septoria leaf spot/blotch on tomato.
